# Mortar Smash (mortarsmash.com)

> Mortar Smash (formerly titled Brickworks) is a free, plain-English guide for people interested in bricks: brick history, standard brick sizes (UK, US, German, Australian), bond patterns, how clay bricks are made, famous brick buildings, and how to care for and repoint brickwork. It also offers a free brick and mortar calculator and an original brick-smashing browser game of the same name. Guide text and bond diagrams are original. Illustrative photos on the mortar articles are AI-generated and labelled in their captions.

## Guide
- [Brick guide (home)](https://mortarsmash.com/): Overview of everything on the site, with an answer-first summary and FAQ.
- [A short history of bricks](https://mortarsmash.com/#history): From sun-dried mud bricks through fired brick, the Romans and the Industrial Revolution.
- [Brick types and sizes](https://mortarsmash.com/#types): Common, facing, engineering, fire, handmade and perforated bricks, plus a table of national standard sizes.
- [Brick bonds and patterns](https://mortarsmash.com/#bonds): Stretcher, English, Flemish and stack bond, with diagrams.
- [How bricks are made](https://mortarsmash.com/#making): The six steps from digging clay to kiln firing and sorting.
- [Famous brick buildings](https://mortarsmash.com/#famous): Malbork Castle, Hampton Court, the Great Mosque of Djenné, Chilehaus, St Pancras and the Ctesiphon arch.
- [Brick care and repointing tips](https://mortarsmash.com/#care): Mortar choice, raking out, curing, gentle cleaning and fixing damp at the source.
- [Brick FAQ](https://mortarsmash.com/#faq): Short answers on brick sizes, English versus Flemish bond, brickmaking and repointing mortar.

- [Mortar types N, S, M and O](https://mortarsmash.com/mortar-types-n-s-m-o.html): ASTM C270 types for bricklayers — Type N general above-grade, Type S below-grade/retaining, Type M heavy loads, Type O soft historic brick; why harder mortar can damage soft brick.
- [Lime vs cement mortar](https://mortarsmash.com/lime-vs-cement-mortar.html): Lime, NHL and Portland cement binders compared; when soft brick needs lime; cement-lime Type N/S as the practical middle; curing differences.
- [How to mix mortar](https://mortarsmash.com/how-to-mix-mortar.html): Volume ratios 1:3 to 1:6, cement:lime:sand gauging, water sense, batch size, wheelbarrow vs mixer, and common strength failures.
- [Building sand vs sharp sand](https://mortarsmash.com/building-sand-vs-sharp-sand.html): Masonry sand (building sand, ASTM C144) versus sharp or concrete sand (ASTM C33) for bricklaying mortar, floor beds, and concrete, with illustrative volume ratios.

- [Trade guides hub](https://mortarsmash.com/guides.html): Index of all bricklaying and mortar guides.
- [Cold weather bricklaying](https://mortarsmash.com/cold-weather-bricklaying.html): Cold weather bricklaying rules: when the 40 °F threshold applies, how warm mortar must be, and how long to cover new brickwork, from BIA and TMS guidance.
- [Hot weather bricklaying](https://mortarsmash.com/hot-weather-bricklaying.html): Hot weather bricklaying: the 100 °F and 90 °F with wind thresholds, the 2 hour mortar limit, fog spraying, shade and cool water, per BIA Technical Note 1.
- [How long mortar stays usable](https://mortarsmash.com/how-long-is-mortar-workable.html): Use mixed mortar within 2½ hours, or 2 hours in hot weather. When retempering with water is fine, and when it is not: colored and repointing mortar.
- [Efflorescence on brick](https://mortarsmash.com/efflorescence-on-brick.html): White powder on brick is usually efflorescence: salts carried out by water. How to tell it from lime run, remove it, and stop it coming back.
- [Cleaning new brickwork](https://mortarsmash.com/how-to-clean-new-brickwork.html): Clean new brickwork safely: when to start, soak the wall first, test a 20 sq ft patch, keep cleaner under 50 psi and rinse under 400 psi.
- [Mortar joint profiles](https://mortarsmash.com/mortar-joint-profiles.html): Concave, V and grapevine joints resist rain best on exterior brick. How raked, struck and flush joints compare, and when mortar is thumbprint hard.
- [How to repoint brick](https://mortarsmash.com/how-to-repoint-brick.html): Repointing brick step by step: fix the cause, rake out 2 to 2½ times the joint width, use a softer matching mortar and fill in ¼ inch layers.
- [Weep holes in brick walls](https://mortarsmash.com/weep-holes-in-brick.html): Weep holes drain water from behind brick. BIA recommends open head joint weeps no more than 24 in apart, right above the flashing. Never block them.
- [Mortar joint thickness](https://mortarsmash.com/mortar-joint-thickness.html): Standard brick mortar joints are 3/8 in (9.5 mm) for US modular brick and 10 mm in UK work. How joint size sets brick sizes and coursing.
- [Colored mortar](https://mortarsmash.com/colored-mortar.html): Colored mortar: ASTM C979 pigments, max 10% of cement weight for metallic oxides and 2% for carbon black. How to batch for even color.
- [Mortar vs grout vs concrete](https://mortarsmash.com/mortar-vs-grout-vs-concrete.html): Mortar bonds brick (ASTM C270), masonry grout fills cores (ASTM C476) and concrete is structural with coarse aggregate. Uses and timing compared.

## Tools
- [Brick calculator](https://mortarsmash.com/brick-calculator.html): Estimates bricks, wet mortar, cement and sand for a wall in UK, US modular, German NF, Australian or custom sizes, and shows the working. Includes one-click common-project presets, a "bricks for common jobs" table, and a US answer block on how many bricks per square foot (modular ~6.9/sq ft single leaf; 20 ft × 3 ft two-wythe seat wall worked example), and a brick pier and pillar calculator (UK 1½-brick pier ~4½ bricks per course, ~60 per metre; US modular 12 and 16 in piers), and a brick-on-edge coping section (~13⅓ UK bricks per metre on a 215 mm wall; US rowlock cap ~4.6 per ft), and a garden wall footing concrete section (~0.1 m³ per metre for a 215 mm wall on a 450 × 225 mm strip; US 16 × 8 in footing ~0.9 cu ft per ft), and a concrete block section (~10 UK 440 × 215 mm blocks per m²; US 8 × 8 × 16 in CMU 1.125 per sq ft), and a brick weight section (UK brick ~2.2–3.4 kg, ~2.5–3 t per 1,000; US modular ~3.5 lb cored, 4.5 lb solid).
- [Mortar calculator](https://mortarsmash.com/mortar-calculator.html): Wet mortar, cement and sand from a brick count or wall area (UK, US modular, German NF, Australian). About 0.3 m³ wet mortar, five 25 kg cement bags and ~0.5 t sand per 1,000 UK bricks in a half-brick wall at 1:4 with 10% waste; per-100 bricks answer (~30 L wet mortar, ~11 kg cement, ~50 kg sand for 100 UK bricks) and ready-mixed bag guide; per-1,000 and per-m² table; mix ratio guide (1:3 to 1:6, US Types N/S/M).

## Game
- [Mortar Smash](https://mortarsmash.com/game.html): A free, original brick-smashing arcade game with 9 levels and keyboard, mouse and touch controls.
